description: Declare core + per-purpose extension groups once, then create and check VS Code profiles from that preset
config.title: Profile Kit
config.preset: The preset itself (core extensions, groups, profiles, settings), stored in Settings so Settings Sync takes it to your other PCs. Used instead of `#profileKit.presetPath#` when set. Edit it with **Profile Kit: Edit Preset**; **Store Preset in Settings (Sync)** puts a preset file here.
config.presetPath: Preset file (`*.profile-kit.json`) that declares core extensions, groups, profiles and settings. The same file is used in every profile. It is a path on this PC, so Settings Sync does not copy it to other PCs; to use one preset on several PCs, store it in Settings (`#profileKit.preset#`).
config.profile: Written by Profile Kit into each profile's own settings: the profile's name, so Profile Kit can tell which profile a window uses. Do not edit.
config.managedKeys: Written by Profile Kit into each profile's own settings: the keys it manages there, so it can update or remove only those. It is kept in the same file so it moves with Settings Sync. Do not edit.

walkthrough.title: Get Started with Profile Kit
walkthrough.description: Set up VS Code profiles from one preset file: what every profile gets, and what each one adds.
walkthrough.preset.title: Pick a preset
walkthrough.preset.description:
A preset is one file that lists the extensions every profile gets (core), named groups, and the profiles built from them. Start from a built-in one (the one that fits this PC is recommended) or from the extensions of this profile.
[Start from a Built-in Preset](command:profileKit.startFromStarter)
[Create from This Profile](command:profileKit.createPreset)
Already have one, for example in a repository? [Open the preset file](command:profileKit.openPreset).
walkthrough.preset.alt: A preset file: core extensions, groups, and the profiles built from them.
walkthrough.apply.title: Create the profiles
walkthrough.apply.description:
Applying creates the profiles that do not exist yet, installs missing extensions and writes the preset settings. You see every change first. Nothing is uninstalled and the Default profile is not changed. VS Code opens a window for each new profile; close it once the profile is there.
[Apply Preset to All Profiles](command:profileKit.applyAll)
walkthrough.apply.alt: One preset file creating three profiles.
walkthrough.switch.title: Switch profiles
walkthrough.switch.description:
Click the profile name in the status bar: the list switches this window, and every other Profile Kit action is below it. When a folder looks like one of your profiles (for example pyproject.toml for Python), Profile Kit suggests it once.
[Show Profiles and Actions](command:profileKit.menu)
walkthrough.switch.alt: The profile name in the status bar and the list of profiles to switch to.
walkthrough.install.title: Add extensions to profiles
walkthrough.install.description:
Install extensions as usual: Profile Kit asks which other profiles should get one, with the suggested ones checked, and records it in the preset. To see and change everything at once, open the manager: extensions × profiles, and settings.
[Install to Profiles](command:profileKit.installToProfiles)
[Open Manager](command:profileKit.openManager)
walkthrough.install.alt: An extension added to two of three profiles.
